HUEvRyemKSg.title: 28c3: The coming war on general computation
HUEvRyemKSg.summary: Cory Doctorow's 28c3 keynote argues that the copyright wars were just a skirmish and that the real fight will be a war on the general-purpose computer. He explains why locked-down devices, DRM and surveillance tools all depend on removing general computation.
HUEvRyemKSg.why: HN returns to it constantly as a prescient talk, cited whenever threads cover DRM, locked-down devices, app verification or restrictions on running your own software.

quote.text: which I very strongly recommend that everybody watch

GnBbhXBDmwU.title: LibreSSL with Bob Beck
GnBbhXBDmwU.summary: Bob Beck of OpenBSD describes the first month of LibreSSL, the fork aimed at cleaning up OpenSSL, including oddities found in the code base and why it was cleaned rather than audited cryptographically.
GnBbhXBDmwU.why: Frequently linked as an entertaining and alarming account of OpenSSL code quality and why the fork happened.

categories.name: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

quote.text: The entire talk is amazing, even 7 years later.

KAWA1DuvCnQ.title: Dconf 2014 Day 2 Keynote: The Last Thing D Needs -- Scott Meyers
KAWA1DuvCnQ.summary: Scott Meyers' keynote at DConf 2014, drawing on 25 years of C++ experience to offer the D language community a plea about what it should avoid. It centers on the accumulated complexity and pitfalls of C++ as a cautionary tale.
KAWA1DuvCnQ.why: HN commenters bring it up whenever C++ complexity or the pitfalls of language design come up, as a witty and authoritative warning.

categories.name: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

quote.text: everyone should watch Scott Meyers's awesome presentation at a D conference

hEx5DNLWGgA.title: CppCon 2015: Herb Sutter "Writing Good C++14... By Default"
hEx5DNLWGgA.summary: Herb Sutter's CppCon 2015 plenary on writing safe, modern C++ by default using the C++ Core Guidelines. It includes a demo of lifetime-checking static analysis tooling.
hEx5DNLWGgA.why: HN cites it in C++ versus Rust safety debates for its lifetime profile demo, and recommends it as a modern C++ talk.

v_UyVmITiYQ.title: Google Wave Developer Preview at Google I/O 2009

v_UyVmITiYQ.why: HN returns to it as the original Wave pitch, both for its wow factor and as a case study in a hyped product that was later shut down.

HipTO_7mUOw.title: Slaughterbots

Jv7sLrON7QY.title: The Psychology of Human Misjudgement - Charlie Munger Full Speech
Jv7sLrON7QY.summary: A recording of Charlie Munger's 1995 Harvard speech on the psychology of human misjudgment. He walks through a list of cognitive biases such as incentives, social proof, and overoptimism.
Jv7sLrON7QY.why: HN recommends it as an insightful catalog of the biases that drive bad decisions, and links it often in Munger memorials and self-improvement threads.

quote.text: heres his talk explaining some of his excellent theories

_loUDS4c3Cs.title: Moon Landings Faked? Filmmaker Says Not!
_loUDS4c3Cs.summary: A filmmaker explains why the Apollo moon landing footage could not have been faked in a studio, based on the video and film technology of the late 1960s. He walks through the limits of cameras, frame rates and effects of the era.
_loUDS4c3Cs.why: HN points to it as a concise, technically grounded rebuttal to moon-hoax claims.

quote.text: This video goes through why the video technology at the time simply wasn't even good enough to enable faking the moon landing.

wbp-3BJWsU8.title: Google I/O 2011: Java Puzzlers - Scraping the Bottom of the Barrel
wbp-3BJWsU8.summary: Josh Bloch and Jeremy Manson present the eighth installment of Java Puzzlers at Google I/O 2011, a set of surprising corner cases in the Java language and libraries. It includes puzzlers on traps such as regular expression performance.
wbp-3BJWsU8.why: HN commenters recommend it as an entertaining tour of exotic Java corner cases.

quote.text: Java Puzzlers by Joshua Bloch and Jeremy Manson are pretty entertaining.
